NEW-GS-U6-1527.q: The Adichanallur archaeological site is on the banks of which river?
NEW-GS-U6-1527.e: Adichanallur is in Thoothukudi district on the banks of the Thamirabarani; burial urns (mudhumakkal thazhi) were found there. Keezhadi (Sivagangai district) is on the Vaigai.

NEW-GS-U6-1528.q: Which archaeological site near Puducherry has yielded evidence of trade with the Romans?
NEW-GS-U6-1528.e: Arikamedu near Puducherry was an Indo-Roman trading port; Mortimer Wheeler excavated it in 1945 and found Roman (Arretine) pottery, beads and more. Kodumanal is in Erode district, Uraiyur in Tiruchirappalli and Keezhadi in Sivagangai district.

NEW-GS-U6-1529.q: The famous port of the Sangam-age Cholas was
NEW-GS-U6-1529.e: The Chola port was Kaveripoompattinam (Puhar); their capital was Uraiyur. Korkai was the Pandya port; Musiri and Thondi were Chera ports.

NEW-GS-U6-1530.q: The capital of the Sangam-age Cheras was
NEW-GS-U6-1530.e: The Chera capital was Vanji (identified with present-day Karur). Madurai – Pandyas; Uraiyur – Cholas; Kanchi – the later Pallava capital.

NEW-GS-U6-1531.q: A stone erected in memory of a warrior who died in battle is called
NEW-GS-U6-1531.e: A stone set up in memory of a warrior killed in battle is a nadukal (hero stone); Tolkappiyam and Sangam literature describe hero-stone worship.

o: Mountains and the land around them
Forests and the land around them
Fields and the land around them
The sea and the land around it
NEW-GS-U6-1532.e: Neithal – the sea and the coastal land around it. Kurinji – mountains; Mullai – forest; Marutham – fields; Palai – parched, sandy land.

NEW-GS-U6-1533.q: The oldest extant grammar work in Tamil is
NEW-GS-U6-1533.e: Tolkappiyam by Tolkappiyar is the oldest Tamil grammar available today (three sections: Ezhuthu, Sol, Porul). Nannool – Pavanandhi Munivar (later); Yapparungalak Karigai – Amithasagarar; Thandiyalangaram – Thandi.

NEW-GS-U6-1534.q: The author of the epic Manimekalai is
NEW-GS-U6-1534.e: Manimekalai – Seethalai Sathanar. Silappathikaram – Ilango Adigal; Seevaka Sinthamani – Thiruthakkadevar; Kambaramayanam – Kambar. Silappathikaram and Manimekalai are called the 'twin epics'.

NEW-GS-U6-1535.q: Which of these is NOT one of the Five Great Epics (Aimperumkappiyangal)?
NEW-GS-U6-1535.e: The Five Great Epics are Silappathikaram, Manimekalai, Seevaka Sinthamani, Valayapathi and Kundalakesi. Perungathai (by Konguvelir) is not among them.

NEW-GS-U6-1536.e: Periya Puranam, the lives of the 63 Nayanmars, was written by Sekkizhar (time of Kulothunga Chola II). Nambiyandar Nambi compiled the Thirumurai; Thiruvasagam – Manikkavasagar.

NEW-GS-U6-1537.q: How many chapters (adhikarams) are there in the Porutpal of the Thirukkural?
NEW-GS-U6-1537.e: Thirukkural has 133 chapters and 1330 couplets: Arathuppal 38, Porutpal 70 and Kamathuppal (Inbathuppal) 25 chapters (38 + 70 + 25 = 133).

NEW-GS-U6-1538.q: The total height (with pedestal) of the Thiruvalluvar statue at Kanyakumari is
NEW-GS-U6-1538.e: The Thiruvalluvar statue at Kanyakumari is 133 feet tall in all, for the Kural's 133 chapters: a 38-foot pedestal (Arathuppal's 38 chapters) and a 95-foot statue. It was unveiled on 1 January 2000.

NEW-GS-U6-1539.q: Who translated the Arathuppal and Porutpal of the Thirukkural into Latin?
NEW-GS-U6-1539.e: Veeramamunivar (Constantine Joseph Beschi) translated the first two parts of the Kural into Latin. G.U. Pope translated it into English; Caldwell wrote 'A Comparative Grammar of the Dravidian Languages'; Ziegenbalg set up a printing press at Tharangambadi.

NEW-GS-U6-1540.q: The Vellore Mutiny took place in
NEW-GS-U6-1540.e: On 10 July 1806 Indian sepoys revolted in Vellore Fort; new rules on uniform and headgear were the immediate cause. 1799 – Kattabomman hanged; 1801 – the Marudhu brothers hanged; 1857 – the Great Revolt.

NEW-GS-U6-1541.q: Who led the 1930 salt satyagraha march from Tiruchirappalli to Vedaranyam?
NEW-GS-U6-1541.e: Following Gandhiji's Dandi March, Rajaji (C. Rajagopalachari) led a salt satyagraha march from Tiruchirappalli to Vedaranyam in 1930 and broke the salt law.

NEW-GS-U6-1542.q: Who is honoured as 'Kodi Kaatha Kumaran' (Kumaran who saved the flag)?
NEW-GS-U6-1542.e: In January 1932, during the Civil Disobedience Movement, Tiruppur Kumaran was beaten in a police lathi charge on a procession in Tiruppur but died still holding the national flag, so he is called 'Kodi Kaatha Kumaran'.

NEW-GS-U6-1543.q: In 1911, Tirunelveli Collector Ashe was shot dead at Maniyachi railway station by
NEW-GS-U6-1543.e: On 17 June 1911 Vanchinathan shot Collector Robert Ashe at Maniyachi railway station and then took his own life. Ashe had played a part in crushing V.O.C.'s shipping company.

NEW-GS-U6-1544.q: Puli Thevar, one of the earliest palayakkarars to resist the British, belonged to which palayam?
NEW-GS-U6-1544.e: Puli Thevar was the palayakkarar of Nerkattumseval (in present-day Tenkasi district). Panchalankurichi – Veerapandiya Kattabomman; Sivagangai – Velu Nachiyar and the Marudhu brothers.

NEW-GS-U6-1545.q: The South Indian Liberal Federation (Justice Party) was founded in
NEW-GS-U6-1545.e: Dr T.M. Nair, P. Theagaraya Chetty, C. Natesanar and others founded the South Indian Liberal Federation in 1916; it was called the Justice Party after its paper 'Justice'. 1920 – the Justice Party formed its first ministry; 1925 – the Self-Respect Movement.

NEW-GS-U6-1546.q: Who is called 'Vaikom Veerar' (Hero of Vaikom)?
NEW-GS-U6-1546.e: Periyar is called 'Vaikom Veerar' for joining, and being jailed in, the 1924–25 Vaikom struggle in Kerala for the right of oppressed castes to use the temple streets.

NEW-GS-U6-1547.q: Where did Ramalinga Adigal (Vallalar) set up the 'Sathya Dharma Salai' to feed the hungry?
NEW-GS-U6-1547.e: Vallalar founded the Sathya Dharma Salai at Vadalur in 1867; the hearth he lit is said to be burning still. He was born at Marudur; the Sathya Gnana Sabha is also at Vadalur.

NEW-GS-U6-1548.q: E.V. Ramasamy was given the title 'Periyar' at
o: The 1938 Tamil Nadu Women's Conference in Chennai
NEW-GS-U6-1548.e: At the Tamil Nadu Women's Conference in Chennai in November 1938, E.V.R. was given the title 'Periyar'. 1929 – the first Self-Respect Conference at Chengalpattu; 1944 – at Salem the Justice Party became the Dravidar Kazhagam; 1925 – Periyar walked out of the Kanchipuram Congress conference.
